sourcesReviewed.role: Singapore-market English-language nickname reference; reviewed the named model/reference explanations and market context.
Official Singapore configuration and exact modelReference/dial evidence used to constrain nickname applicability; official names were not treated as nicknames.

acceptedCollectionAliases.name: President
acceptedCollectionAliases.reason: The Singapore-market article identifies President as a Rolex nickname associated with the Day-Date/President bracelet family; retained as a collection-level alias rather than applied to every configuration as a configuration nickname.

acceptedLocalNicknames.name: Panda
acceptedLocalNicknames.reason: The source describes the modern Daytona white-dial/black-counter-ring configuration as Panda; the official Singapore observation for m126500ln-0001 confirms that exact visual configuration.

acceptedLocalNicknames.name: Batgirl
acceptedLocalNicknames.reason: The source identifies 126710BLNR with a Jubilee bracelet as Batgirl; the official Singapore product page for m126710blnr-0002 confirms the Jubilee bracelet.

acceptedLocalNicknames.name: Starbucks
acceptedLocalNicknames.reason: The source explicitly identifies Ref. 126610LV as Starbucks; the official Singapore observation maps that reference family to m126610lv-0002.

acceptedLocalNicknames.name: Root Beer

sourceQuotes: The Panda nickname refers to modern Rolex Daytona models that feature a white dial with black sub dials.
The Batgirl is the nickname for the Rolex GMT-Master II Ref. 126710BLNR, which features the same blue and black bezel as the Batman but comes with a Jubilee bracelet.
The Submariner Ref. 126610LV introduced in 2020 is often called the Starbucks.
Root Beer is the nickname for GMT-Master models with a brown and gold bezel, including Ref. 1675/3 and the modern 126711CHNR.
The James Cameron Deepsea is a Rolex Sea-Dweller with a gradient blue-to-black dial called D-Blue.
Some names like ‘President’ refer to an actual Rolex bracelet and are officially used by the brand.
notes: The research was intentionally conservative. One Singapore-market source was sufficient for accepted names without claiming frequency or universal usage; no claim of an Internet-wide top-five ranking is made.
